title: 35th Street and the Mecca flat in Chicago
summary: Talk of Chicago's 35th and State, the Mecca building with all services in one square, and its demolition.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did you ever go to the Dream Land or the Royal Garden or the Lincoln Garden or vacation any other places in Chicago? No.

I used to go to, you know, most places I'd go to right at 35th Street. I don't know what they call that place. I forgot a name what they call it. 35th Street. It's right across from the Mecca building. Mecca flat? Yeah, Mecca flat.

Yeah, all that's tore down, huh? Mm-hmm. Yeah, all that's tore down. All that's tore down. I was up there in 52. It was a shame. They had a hard upon life when they tore Mecca flat down. Yeah, they sure did. They sure did. Famous place. Yeah, sure.
That was a famous corner, 35th and the State. A lot of things. Yeah, yeah.

Yeah, that building had taken in a whole square, you know, them big squares there, you know. And then you didn't have to go out to get anything, just stay right in the house, bring them for you. Your groceries, your doctor, your drug store, it was always in that square. Yeah, they got it. You know, clothes, any kind of clothes you want, you can just go down there and measure them up and tailors and then send them up for you. That's a wonderful place. It's all tore down. It tore down all the way up to the White Sox Park.
Yeah. Maybe we better let it rest a minute now. Mm-hmm.
